To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lipids are a class small molecules with a rich history as biological materials, and that they have recently been investigated as thin film materials exhibiting nano-scale order.

the addition of hard nanoparticles to lipid thin films results in a dramatic increase in the order of the films, and the addition of DNA nucleic acids to lipid thin films induces the formation of a lipid-DNA co-assembled nanostructured film.
lipid thin films can be used as templates to direct the assembly of functional soft and hard materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the fundamental interactions of lipids and other biological molecules with substrates.
the development and characterization of soft materials that are capable of controlling the assembly of functional hard materials into well-defined, nanostructured architectures.

developing a fundamental understanding of the interactions between lipid nanostructured substrata and functional molecules and particles with the goal of creating novel functional materials for applications in nanotechnology and biotechnology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of lipid nanostructures on solid substrates is in its infancy and that the potential for the field to grow is tremendous.
lipids are a soft matter system that can serve as a platform for directing the self-assembly of hard materials into nanostructured thin films.
the field of lipid soft matter is a rapidly expanding area with a wide range of potential applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lipid system provides a rich platform to develop and control nanostructured materials for the assembly of functional soft materials.
lipid nanostructured films can direct and organize the self-assembly of functional materials.
the introduction of a substrate to lipid systems results in the formation of a new class of materials that can be used for the directed assembly and patterning of functional materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lipid thin films can be utilized as a platform for directing the assembly, orientation, and organization of other functional materials.
lipid nanostructure can be tuned by the introduction of hard materials and that these nanostructured lipid films have the capacity to direct the assembly of hard materials.
lipids are a powerful soft-matter system for directing the assembly and organization of hard materials.
